item.title: Melania Trump hosts Ukraine, Russia officials, calls for ‘more enduring’ truce
item.description: Melania ⁠Trump, US President Donald Trump’s wife, joined representatives ⁠from Russia and Ukraine on Thursday at a White House event to recognise a recent six-day ceasefire she helped broker in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky. The event followed US officials’ ramped-up efforts to secure a deal to end the conflict between Russia and ‌Ukraine, which began when Russian forces invaded Ukraine in early 2022. item.title: Paraguay’s President Pena resigns under mounting pressure from bank collapse
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago ⁠Pena resigned ⁠on Thursday as calls ⁠for his removal swelled following the collapse of digital lender Ueno that left millions of customers unable to access their accounts. “I do so with the stability of our country, ‌social peace, and the need to preserve our democratic institutions in mind,” he said in a video recorded address on Thursday. item.title: Hong Kong police arrest operator of prisoner support group over allegedly seditious books
item.description: Hong Kong national security police have arrested an operator of a local prisoner support group on suspicion of importing seditious publications, days after the group revealed that customs had seized dozens of books it had ordered from Taiwan. Police said officers carried out an enforcement operation in Mong Kok on Thursday morning, arresting a local man, 34, on suspicion of “importing a publication that has a seditious intention”, an offence under the Safeguarding National Security...

item.title: Iran says 5 tankers catch fire after striking naval mines in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and army said in separate statements, according to local media on Thursday. Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. item.title: After US$474m gamble flops, what happens now to Elon Musk’s Tesla, SpaceX and China ties?
item.description: Elon Musk bet nearly half a billion dollars that political spending could keep Washington friendly to his sprawling business empire. On Tuesday, that bet came up short. As Democrats recaptured control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, the world’s richest man found himself facing an abruptly altered political landscape.
